objective.statement: Read and write notes in the tenor clef, whose middle C is on the fourth line.
successCriteria: I know the tenor clef is a C clef centred on the fourth line.
I can find middle C and name notes around it.
I do not mix up the tenor clef and the alto clef.

explanation.text: The tenor clef is another C clef, like the alto clef you already know. A C clef is drawn so that the middle of the sign marks middle C. The only difference between the two is where the sign is centred: the alto clef is centred on the middle (third) line, and the tenor clef is centred on the fourth line from the bottom. So in the tenor clef, middle C is on the fourth line.

music.textAlternative: A tenor-clef stave with one semibreve, middle C, on the fourth line from the bottom.

explanation.caption: Tenor clef: middle C is on the fourth line.

explanation.text: From middle C you can count to any other note, one letter for each line and space. The line below is A, the space above is D, the top line is E. The bottom line of the tenor clef is D, a seventh below middle C; the lines are D, F, A, C and E, from the bottom up.

music.textAlternative: A tenor-clef stave with five semibreves on the five lines: D, F, A, C, E.

explanation.caption: The five lines of the tenor clef, from the bottom: D F A C E.

explanation.text: The treble clef covers the highest notes, the alto clef lower ones, the tenor clef lower still, and the bass clef the lowest of all. The tenor clef is used by cellos, bassoons and tenor trombones for their higher notes; it is no longer used for singers. Because the alto and tenor clefs look so alike, always check which one is printed before you name a note.
Alto: middle C on the middle line. Tenor: middle C on the fourth line, one line higher. Find middle C first, then count.

music.textAlternative: A tenor-clef stave with one semibreve on the top line.

steps: Find middle C: the fourth line.

demonstration.textAlternative: A note on the top line of the tenor clef is E.

third.reason: Middle C is on the middle line in the alto clef. The tenor clef is centred one line higher: on the fourth line.

first.reason: The bottom line is the first line. In the bass clef middle C is above the stave; in the tenor clef it is on the fourth line.

second.reason: In the tenor clef middle C is on the fourth line: the clef's centre is drawn on that line.

fifth.reason: The tenor clef is centred on the fourth line, so middle C is there, not on the top line.

independent.prompt: Which of these instruments can read the tenor clef (as well as the bass clef)?

viola.reason: No: the viola reads the alto clef (and sometimes the treble).

bass trombone.reason: No: the bass trombone reads the bass clef.

double bassoon.reason: No: the double bassoon reads the bass clef.
